searchText: Hey guys, Im sorry if its the wrong place to ask this, but why do uncle blocks rewarded in ethereum blockchain, but orphaned blocks on bitcoin are not rewarded. Im looking to learn a bit more on this eth has 13-15 second block time, bitcoin has 10 minute. its possible for eth miners to accidentally mine uncles due to a few seconds of communication latency, so they are also rewarded to smooth variability in rewards. not so for bitcoin miners Okay, that brings me to another question, why does eth have variable blocktime? that is a target and is a parameter set in a mining protocol. mining is a poission process around that target. Bitcoin has variable block time as well Is there a resource with the list of all operations that can be done are listed with their fixed gas limits? I want to learn why those operations have been fixed with that specific gas limit. (ex : addition requires 4 gas, sending transactions has 21000 gas limit etc) https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf gives the values. The "why" is generally down the relative amount of resources used by the opcode (for some theoretical combined cpu/storage resource)
